1.title: FROST ON THE GROUND
1.text: Thin water-ice frost forms on Mars on cold nights. NASA's Viking 2 lander photographed frost on the ground in 1979.

2.title: WATER HIDING IN SOIL
2.text: Mars soil holds water locked inside its minerals. Curiosity's first soil sample in 2012 was about 2% water.

3.title: A RADIATION RECORD
3.text: Curiosity's RAD instrument has measured radiation on the ground of Mars since 2012. That helps plan how to protect astronauts.

4.title: A ROCK FROM AN OLD LAKE
4.text: Curiosity found rocks that formed in an ancient lake in Gale Crater. Long ago, water stayed on Mars for a long time.

5.title: A DUST DEVIL
5.text: Whirlwinds called dust devils cross Mars. Sometimes they blew dust off rover solar panels and gave them more power.

6.title: AURORA OVER MARS
6.text: During the May 2024 solar storm, NASA's MAVEN orbiter saw auroras glowing across Mars. Mars has auroras even without a global magnetic field.

7.title: A BULALAKAW!
7.text: Space rocks hit Mars more often than Earth because its air is so thin. NASA's InSight lander even felt meteoroid impacts as marsquakes.

requests.text: The battery cells are cold. Can I warm them up? It costs a little power, but I'll find spare parts too!
Can I go outside to tighten a loose solar panel? I'll bring back spare parts.
The plants look sad. Can I switch on the Crop Lamp for them?
Can I run a soil experiment? It uses some power, but we might learn something!
Can I use a spare oxygen tank to check everyone's suits? It keeps the crew safe and happy.
Can I take the crew's health readings? It uses a little power for the scanner.
Can I go outside to fix the antenna? I need to walk out to the dish.
Can I charge my suit batteries now? It uses power, but my next walk outside will be safer.
